intent.note: Clause by clause. "Fix it with ONE shared rule both surfaces use, not a second copy ... put the disclosure-arrow rule in the shared layer": matches. New ui/shared/disclosure.css holds `:where(.fdetails)>summary::after{content:"\25BE";content:"\25BE" / "";...}`, the [open] variant and the ::-webkit-details-marker hide. It is joined into both _ui_theme.REPORT_CSS_PARTS (first) and PANEL_CSS_PARTS (after tokens-and-reset.css). cs8/cs9 hold the two tuples to the same shared list read first, and cs2/cs5 count it as declared. "Remove the per-surface copies": matches. The copies are gone from controls.css and usage-tab.css; a grep of plugins/audit/scripts for `summary::after|25BE|25B4|details-marker` outside shared/disclosure.css returns nothing, and da1 and uf7 count exactly two `>summary::after{` rules per sheet. "the glyph must not be exposed to assistive tech ... choose one that works in forced-colors, and say which and why": matches. It is a text glyph with an empty alt, and disclosure.css's header comment says why: forced colours repaint text instead of dropping it. ax5 drives that in forced colours on the report. "Prove it: a browser check ... red-first on the current panel and report": diverges. ax4 (report, check-report-interactive.mjs) and pa1 (panel, capture-screenshots.mjs, which --check does drive through assertUsageWorks) exist and ran green in the recorded gate, but no red was ever recorded for them (finding 1). "Refresh followers": matches. acme html/md, demo-large, index and screenshots are in the diff. "No register ids in comments": matches, none found. The sd5 retry also matches the context's ask: sd5 now requires `_missing_ui_parts(...)` to name a part listed under ui/ rather than the literal `shell.css`. I ran test__surface_digest.py --selftest once: exit 0, 8/8, sd5 names ['shared/disclosure.css']. Claim vs diff: outcome.technical describes the diff accurately, including that the report-side tests.add rows map to pre-existing is1-is9. But the filed `casesAdded` lists is1-is9 (present at HEAD: grep counts equal at HEAD and in the tree) and leaves out the cases this task actually added (pa1, ph1-ph5 are partly listed; ax4, ax5, da1, cs8, cs9 and the sd5 rewrite are not). So `casesAdded` does not describe the diff. Beyond the clause: ph1-ph5 (assertUsageHoverParity) answer the brief's tests.add rows for usage-tab.css and are in scope.
intent.redFirstBasis: Executor's word for attempt 2 is `not-attempted`, with a basis covering only sd5. That basis does show sd5 red by two in-place mutations of the error text (exit 1 each, restored cmp-equal). Attempt 1's word is `could-not-prove`: the red-first helper refused usage-tab.css as an inline suite. Nothing handed shows ax4, ax5 or pa1 failing on any tree, and the description explicitly asks for that red. On the report, HEAD already had the empty alternative, so a HEAD run of ax4 would be green. tests.expectRedFirst false makes `not-attempted` the schema-default word, but it does not hold against the description's own red-first clause.
